papers.title: Niche-driven divergence of prokaryotic and viral communities in Pogonatum cirratum.
papers.abstract: Ecological niche partitioning shapes microbial communities in terrestrial mosses, yet its underlying mechanisms and associated viral diversity remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil (Rs) and endophytic niche (Pc) of Pogonatum cirratum using amplicon and metagenomic sequencing. Rs exhibited higher species richness, co-dominated by Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, and Actinomycetota, whereas Pc was dominated by Pseudomonadota (81.13%) but showed greater functional diversity. Source tracking revealed that 10.57% of Pc taxa origin
papers.summary: This study characterizes the prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil and endophytic niche of the moss Pogonatum cirratum, revealing distinct niche-driven divergence. The endophytic niche shows lower species richness but higher functional diversity, with a small proportion of taxa sourced from the soil, and the associated viral communities also differ between niches.

papers.title: Longitudinal Exploratory Analysis of Salivary Microbiota Profiles in Patients with Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Before and After Surgery: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Salivary microbiome profiling may represent a promising non-invasive approach for characterizing OSCC-associated microbial patterns and longitudinal microbiome dynamics during patient management. This exploratory pilot study aimed to longitudinally assess salivary microbiota profiles in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) before and after tumor resection using Oxford Nanopore Technology. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 16 patients with OSCC at two time points (before and after tumor resection) and from 10 OSCC-free reference subjects. Microbial DNA was extracted u
papers.summary: This pilot study used Oxford Nanopore Technology to longitudinally profile salivary microbiota in 16 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) patients before and after tumor resection, comparing them to 10 healthy controls. The findings suggest that salivary microbiome profiles may shift after surgery, highlighting the potential of non-invasive salivary sampling for monitoring OSCC-associated microbial changes.

papers.title: Distinct gut microbiome profiles characterize obese and non-obese patients with atherosclerosis: a metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Obesity is widely recognized as an aggravating risk factor for atherosclerosis (AS), yet the effects of obesity on AS-associated microbiome dysbiosis are not sufficiently characterized. This study aims to identify the contribution of obesity-related dysbiosis in AS.
papers.summary: This study compares the gut microbiome of obese and non-obese patients with atherosclerosis using metagenomic analysis, revealing distinct microbial profiles associated with each group. The findings suggest that obesity contributes to specific gut microbiome dysbiosis patterns in atherosclerosis, potentially informing more personalized therapeutic approaches.

papers.title: A Sample to Results Workflow for Compositional Analysis of Multiplexed Amplicon Sequencing Experiments.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities play key roles in the transformation and cycling of elements ranging from required macronutrients to toxic metalloids. Next-generation sequencing has been applied across multiple ecosystems to probe the interplay of microbial community structure and functional potential with respect to elemental cycling. Shotgun metagenomics collects marker gene sequences without amplification and is costly for large numbers of samples and deep coverage. Conversely, amplicon sequencing of taxonomic marker genes, e.g. 16S and 18S rRNA, is cost-effective for large numbers of samples, but pr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a streamlined sample-to-results workflow for analyzing multiplexed amplicon sequencing data, focusing on compositional analysis of microbial communities. The workflow aims to provide a cost-effective alternative to shotgun metagenomics for large-scale studies, enabling efficient processing of 16S/18S rRNA amplicon data.

papers.title: Clinical Improvement and Taxonomic-Functional Gut Microbiome Remodeling After Six Months of Multi-Strain Synbiotic Supplementation in Mexican Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gut dysbiosis in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been associated with alterations in microbial ecology and metabolic function that may contribute to gastrointestinal dysfunction and the severity of clinical manifestations. Synbiotic and probiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising microbiome-targeted strategy for ASD; however, its effects on gut microbiome composition, functional potential, and clinical outcomes remain incompletely understood. We conducted a longitudinal study of Mexican children diagnosed with ASD to analyze changes in the compo
papers.summary: This longitudinal study in Mexican children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) found that six months of multi-strain synbiotic supplementation led to significant clinical improvement and remodeling of the gut microbiome, including changes in taxonomic composition and functional potential. The results support the potential of synbiotics as a microbiome-targeted intervention to alleviate ASD symptoms and associated gut dysfunction.

papers.title: Microbial metabolite-driven mechanisms linking the gut microbiome to atherosclerosis: multi-omic and translational perspectives.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and a substantial residual risk persists despite optimal management of traditional risk factors. Increasing evidence implicates the gut microbiome as a mechanistic contributor to atherogenesis, not merely through taxonomic shifts but via the production of bioactive microbial metabolites that link diet, microbial metabolism, and host vascular biology. These metabolites have emerged as central effectors of the gut-artery axis, influencing intestinal barrier integrity, systemic immunity, lipid handling, and t
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current evidence on how gut microbiome-derived metabolites contribute to atherosclerosis, emphasizing multi-omic approaches to uncover mechanisms linking diet, microbial metabolism, and vascular biology. It highlights the gut-artery axis as a key pathway influencing inflammation, lipid handling, and immune responses, and discusses translational implications for cardiovascular disease prevention and therapy.

papers.title: Gut microbiome signatures during acute infection are associated with long COVID.
papers.abstract: Long COVID (LC) manifests in 10%-30% of non-hospitalized individuals post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, leading to significant morbidity. The predictive role of gut microbiome composition during acute infection in the development of LC is not well understood, partly because of the heterogeneous nature of the disease.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiome composition during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection can predict the development of long COVID. The authors identify specific microbial signatures associated with subsequent long COVID, suggesting that the gut microbiome may play a role in disease trajectory and could serve as an early biomarker.

papers.title: Environmental selection shapes the ecological cascade of biofilm assembly and functional gene abundance in sandstone weathering.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms are pivotal agents in the process of sandstone weathering; nevertheless, the ecological mechanisms that govern their transition from mere colonization to sustained weathering activity remain ambiguous. This study systematically elucidated microbe-mediated weathering mechanisms through amplicon and metagenomic sequencing of bacteria, fungi, and archaea across a sandstone weathering sequence-from original unweathered sandstone (OS), biofilm-covered sandstone (BS), to weathered sandstone (WS). The findings indicate that microbial communities undergo associations across a weathering
papers.summary: This study uses amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to track microbial communities across a sandstone weathering sequence, revealing that environmental selection drives biofilm assembly and functional gene abundance, ultimately shaping the transition from colonization to active weathering.

papers.title: Large language models enhance annotation of enzymes in metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic data have notable biological potential, but their functional interpretation is frequently impeded by incomplete protein function annotations. Accurate enzyme annotation is essential for elucidating the metabolic capabilities of microbial communities within metagenomic datasets. To address this challenge, we developed FEDKEA, an enzyme annotation tool leveraging protein language models, and provided a web platform for its use. In addition, we designed a user-friendly, FEDKEA-based metagenomic pipeline, MEnzMap, which encompasses the entire analysis workflow-from raw data quality con
papers.summary: The authors developed FEDKEA, an enzyme annotation tool that uses protein language models to improve functional annotation of metagenomic data, and provided a web platform for its use. They also created MEnzMap, a user-friendly pipeline that integrates FEDKEA for complete metagenomic analysis from raw data to enzyme mapping, addressing the bottleneck of incomplete protein function annotations.

papers.title: The gut microbiome organ.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome is increasingly viewed as an active regulator of host physiology, extending beyond earlier taxonomy-centered descriptions of a complex microbial community. Accumulating evidence supports an organ-like conceptual framework in which the gut microbiome exhibits spatially structured organization, extensive metabolic capacity, and continuous bidirectional communication with host systems. Through the production of bioactive metabolites with endocrine-like, immunomodulatory, and neuromodulatory properties, the microbiome contributes to metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine re
papers.summary: This review proposes viewing the gut microbiome as an organ, highlighting its spatially structured organization, metabolic capacity, and bidirectional communication with the host. It emphasizes the microbiome's role in producing bioactive metabolites that influence metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine functions, offering a conceptual framework for understanding its systemic impact.

papers.title: Mapping the causal landscape of polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic Mendelian randomization evidence synthesis and the MR-PCOS atlas platform.
papers.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) studies have increasingly investigated potential predicted antecedents and consequences of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), yet published evidence remains scattered across diverse exposures, outcomes, and analytical frameworks. This study aimed to systematically organize published PCOS-related MR evidence and develop an interactive platform to support evidence retrieval, comparison, and interpretation. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to June 1, 2026. Original MR Studies were eligible if PCOS was either the exposu
papers.summary: This study systematically reviews Mendelian randomization (MR) studies on polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and develops an interactive platform (MR-PCOS atlas) to organize and interpret the scattered evidence. It provides a comprehensive synthesis of potential causal antecedents and consequences of PCOS, supporting evidence retrieval and comparison for researchers.

papers.title: Exploration of the mechanism of gut microbiota-mediated immune modulation in the pathogenesis of pancreatic cancer: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of pancreatic cancer is complex. While immune dysregulation and gut microbiota disturbances are considered key factors, the causal pathway between them remains unclear. This study employs a 2-step Mendelian randomization (MR) approach to empirically investigate the "immune cells - gut microbiota - pancreatic cancer" mediation pathway from a genetic perspective. Relevant data on 731 immune cell phenotypes (N = 3757), 473 gut microbiota (N=8293), and pancreatic cancer (N = 3,87,888) were extracted from large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) and FinnGen summary statisti
papers.summary: This study uses a two-step Mendelian randomization approach to investigate the causal pathway linking gut microbiota, immune cells, and pancreatic cancer risk. The findings suggest that specific gut microbiota may influence pancreatic cancer development through modulation of immune cell phenotypes, providing genetic evidence for a microbiota-immune-cancer axis.

papers.title: Gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and allergic diseases: A bidirectional Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Some authors suggest a link between gut microbiota and allergic diseases; however, the genetically predicted relationship and the role of inflammatory proteins as mediators are still uncertain. Gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 5 types of allergic diseases, namely allergic rhinitis (AR), atopic dermatitis, allergic conjunctivitis, food allergy, and asthma, were identified from large-scale genome-wide association studies summary data. In a 2-sample, bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) study, we systematically conducted 2980 primary tests (298 exposures tested bidirectionally aga
papers.summary: This study uses bidirectional Mendelian randomization to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and five allergic diseases. It finds evidence for specific microbial taxa influencing allergy risk, with some effects potentially mediated by inflammatory proteins, though the overall causal architecture remains complex.

papers.title: The use of multi-species probiotic-derived vesicles to encapsulate luteolin for preventing colitis in a mouse model.
papers.abstract: Probiotic-derived membrane vesicles (MVs) offer advantages over live probiotics, including lower immunogenicity and enhanced bioavailability of dietary compounds. However, their composition and function depend on culture conditions. In this study, MVs from a single probiotic strain (S-MVs) were compared with those from co-cultured multi-species probiotics (M-MVs). M-MVs showed superior radical scavenging ability due to characteristic antioxidant proteins. Luteolin (Lut), a hydrophobic flavonoid, was loaded into M-MVs to generate Lut-MVs. Compared with Lut or M-MVs alone, Lut-MVs had enhanced w
papers.summary: This study shows that membrane vesicles derived from co-cultured multi-species probiotics have superior antioxidant properties compared to those from a single strain, and can effectively encapsulate the flavonoid luteolin. The resulting luteolin-loaded vesicles (Lut-MVs) demonstrated enhanced protective effects against colitis in a mouse model, suggesting a promising strategy for preventing intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: A noninvasive 13C-mannitol breath test to monitor semaglutide treatment-induced delayed oral-cecal transit in mice.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), such as semaglutide, are highly effective treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes but are often associated with gastrointestinal side effects including delayed transit times through the gastrointestinal tract. We present a non-invasive breath test to measure oral-cecal transit time (OCTT) in mice that could be readily translated to clinical studies. Current methods for measuring OCTT are limited by invasiveness, terminal procedures, anesthesia, radioactive tracers, or stress-induced influence on the outcomes. Here we demonstrate that 13C
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
papers.summary: This paper introduces a noninvasive 13C-mannitol breath test to measure oral-cecal transit time (OCTT) in mice, offering a practical alternative to invasive or stressful methods. The test successfully detects delayed gastrointestinal transit induced by semaglutide treatment, and the approach is readily translatable to clinical studies.

papers.title: Age-adjusted machine learning identifies facial skin microbes associated with skin quality among Korean women.
papers.abstract: Recognizing specific microbes that significantly influence skin quality is becoming an essential aspect of personalized skincare. However, conventional large-scale cohort skin microbiome studies often overlook important confounders, such as age, leading to missing meaningful microbe-skin relationships. In this study, we developed an age-adjusted machine learning (AAML) framework to identify microbial candidates associated with skin quality by determining optimal age ranges that enhance age-independent signals of skin microbes. It allowed the identification of distinct age groups that clearly e
papers.summary: This study introduces an age-adjusted machine learning framework to identify facial skin microbes associated with skin quality in Korean women, overcoming the confounding effect of age. By determining optimal age ranges, the framework enhances age-independent microbial signals and reveals distinct microbial candidates linked to skin quality across different age groups.

papers.title: Multi-omics identifies microbial and miRNA biomarkers from rumen fluid for susceptibility of subacute ruminal acidosis in dairy goats.
papers.abstract: With the increasing intensification of animal husbandry, high-concentrate diets are often used in production to ensure high production performance in dairy animals, leading to susceptibility to subacute rumen acidosis (SARA), yet reliable early diagnostic biomarkers remain lacking. In this study, a high-RDS diet was fed to dairy goats as a model, and SARA-tolerant and SARA-susceptible individuals were identified under this diet. By combining 16S rRNA gene sequencing, metagenomic binning, and miRNA transcriptome sequencing, the changes in rumen microbial composition, function, and miRNAs in dai
papers.summary: This study identifies microbial and miRNA biomarkers in rumen fluid that distinguish dairy goats susceptible to subacute ruminal acidosis (SARA) from tolerant ones, using a multi-omics approach combining 16S rRNA sequencing, metagenomic binning, and miRNA transcriptomics. The findings provide potential early diagnostic markers for SARA, which could improve management in high-concentrate feeding systems.

papers.title: Microbiome modelling for post-mortem interval estimation across species and climates: swine analogues in a British summer and external validation in human donors from the USA.
papers.abstract: Background Microbial clocks have shown high accuracy in estimating time since death, or post-mortem interval (PMI), across diverse contexts, including controlled laboratory settings, outdoor environments, and both human cadavers and animal models. However, the limited number of studies performed under different environmental and climatic conditions, particularly in Europe, restricts the broader applicability of these models, as data from distinct climates may not reliably translate across geographic regions. This study investigates the nasal thanatomicrobiome of pig carcasses exposed to outdoo
papers.summary: This study evaluates the use of nasal microbiome 'clocks' to estimate post-mortem interval (PMI) in pig carcasses during a British summer, and tests whether models trained on these swine analogues can be applied to human donor samples from the USA. The findings highlight the challenges of cross-species and cross-climate generalization, emphasizing the need for region- and species-specific models in forensic microbiome applications.

papers.title: AI-Guided Computational Design of Synthetic Microbiota for Next-Generation Immunomodulatory Applications.
papers.abstract: The growing recognition of the human microbiome as a key regulator of immune homeostasis has accelerated the application of computational intelligence for microbiome-driven disease understanding and therapeutic design. However, existing microbiome studies largely rely on classical machine learning or shallow deep learning models that fail to capture higher-order microbial interactions, multimodal functional dependencies, and immune feasibility constraints simultaneously. Moreover, most approaches lack biological constraint enforcement, leading to predictions that may be statistically accurate
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of AI-guided computational design for synthetic microbiota in immunomodulatory applications, highlighting the limitations of current machine learning and deep learning models in capturing complex microbial interactions and enforcing biological constraints. It emphasizes the need for more advanced computational approaches to design effective microbiome-based therapies.

papers.title: First-void urine and cervicovaginal brushes for vaginal microbiome profiling: a proof-of-concept study.
papers.abstract: The human vaginal microbiome is a cornerstone of female reproductive health, influencing susceptibility to vaginal conditions, pregnancy complications, and urogenital infections. Understanding this microbiome is critical for advancing preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic interventions, yet its intimate and dynamic nature poses challenges for accurate, representative, and more inclusive sampling methods. This proof-of-concept study evaluated the performance of first-void urine (FVU) samples and cervicovaginal brushes for vaginal microbiome profiling relative to vaginal swabs. FVU refers to t
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study compares first-void urine and cervicovaginal brushes to standard vaginal swabs for profiling the vaginal microbiome, finding that these alternative sampling methods can provide representative results. The work supports more inclusive and accessible sampling options for studying the vaginal microbiome, which is important for reproductive health research.

papers.title: A Diffusion-Driven CH4-O2 Boundary Structures Methane Oxidation and Carbon Transformation in Upland Soils.
papers.abstract: Although extensive work has characterized high-affinity atmospheric methane oxidation in upland soils and sustained oxidation in chronically methane-rich environments, shallow point-source inputs introduce transient methane pulses into otherwise aerated heterotrophic soils. Whether these pulses migrate rapidly toward the atmosphere or instead create localized redox boundaries that restructure soil carbon pools and microbial metabolism remains unclear. Here, we conducted a controlled natural gas release experiment to quantify coupled geochemical and microbial responses in near-surface soils acr
papers.summary: This study investigates how transient methane pulses in upland soils create localized redox boundaries that influence methane oxidation and carbon transformation. Using a controlled natural gas release experiment, the authors quantify coupled geochemical and microbial responses, revealing that diffusion-driven CH4-O2 boundaries structure microbial metabolism and soil carbon pools.

papers.title: Identification of a Novel Fungal α‑l‑Fucosidase with Transfucosylation Potential.
papers.abstract: Fucosylated carbohydrates are a vital part of human nutrition. They act as prebiotics, nourishing beneficial gut bacteria and helping shape the gut microbiome. Enzymatic synthesis is a convenient method to access these molecules. Fungal α-l-fucosidases are glycoside hydrolases that naturally cleave terminal α-linked fucose residues from glycans; those with synthetic capabilities are conveniently applicable in glycoengineering. This study investigates the fucosylation potential and regioselectivity of rare GH29 α-l-fucosidases from filamentous fungi. The screening of production of putative α-l-
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes a novel fungal α-l-fucosidase from the GH29 family that can synthesize fucosylated carbohydrates, which are important prebiotics for gut health. The enzyme shows transfucosylation potential and specific regioselectivity, making it a promising tool for glycoengineering applications.

papers.title: A Tri-Source Microbiome Dataset from Human Sleep Environments: Saliva, Pillow Dust, and Bedroom Air.
papers.abstract: Despite the established importance of the human microbiome in health, the integrated microbial exposures occurring within the sleep environment remain poorly understood. Sleep represents a critical period of prolonged exposure to indoor microbial reservoirs, yet no study has simultaneously examined the connectivity between environmental sources and the human oral microbiome. We present a novel, tri-source microbiome dataset characterizing microbial communities from co-located saliva, pillow dust, and bedroom air collected from healthy participants in real-world sleep environments. Samples were
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new dataset that simultaneously profiles microbial communities from human saliva, pillow dust, and bedroom air in real-world sleep environments, addressing a gap in understanding integrated microbial exposures during sleep. The tri-source design enables exploration of connections between environmental reservoirs and the human oral microbiome, providing a resource for future studies on sleep-related microbial ecology and health.

papers.title: Joint-RPCA: domain-aware multi-omics integration for systems microbiology.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data is essential for microbiome research, as microbial communities are shaped by and respond to interdependent processes, including taxonomic composition, metabolite production and utilization, and gene expression. However, accurately capturing ecosystem-wide patterns across these modalities is statistically challenging due to differences in scale, sparsity, and compositionality. While a growing number of multi-omics methods have emerged, they differ in their mathematical objectives and modeling assumptions, which in turn shape how biological patterns are represented a
papers.summary: This paper introduces Joint-RPCA, a new computational method for integrating multi-omics data in microbiome research. It addresses the statistical challenges of combining data types with different scales, sparsity, and compositionality, and the authors demonstrate its utility for capturing ecosystem-wide patterns in microbial communities.

papers.title: Promises and Pitfalls of Long-Read Sequencing for Resolving Microbial Complexity.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing (LRS) has driven a transition in microbial genomics, overcoming the assembly fragmentation inherent to short-read sequencing. This review elucidates the impact of LRS across isolate genomics, metagenomics, and multi-omics domains. By spanning extensive repetitive regions, LRS facilitates the reconstruction of circular chromosomes and precisely resolves mobile genetic elements (MGEs). In metagenomics, LRS enables strain-level resolution, the recovery of circular metagenome-assembled genomes, and the precise localization of MGEs within host replicons. Furthermore, the single
papers.summary: This review discusses how long-read sequencing (LRS) has transformed microbial genomics by overcoming short-read assembly limitations, enabling complete circular genomes and precise resolution of mobile genetic elements. It highlights LRS applications in isolate genomics, metagenomics, and multi-omics, while also addressing current challenges and pitfalls, such as higher error rates and cost, that researchers must consider.

papers.title: Prospective associations of tea consumption with skeletal muscle mass and strength: Insights from the gut microbiome and proteomics.
papers.abstract: Tea consumption may be associated with skeletal muscle health, but longitudinal evidence based on repeated assessments remains limited. We examined the associations of tea intake and serum biomarkers with repeated skeletal muscle measures and explored whether these associations might be partly explained by multi-omics features. In this prospective cohort, 3408 adults were followed for approximately 12 years. Skeletal muscle mass was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, handgrip strength by digital dynamometry, gut microbial taxonomic and functional profiles by shotgun metagenomic sequ
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 3,408 adults followed for ~12 years found that tea consumption is associated with better skeletal muscle mass and strength over time. The association appears to be partly mediated by gut microbiome composition and serum proteomic biomarkers, suggesting a multi-omics link between tea intake and muscle health.

papers.title: Environmental filtering shapes biosynthetic potential and resistome of antarctic microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Environmental filtering is a major driver of microbial community assembly in Antarctic ecosystems, yet its influence on biosynthetic potential and antimicrobial resistance remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 319 medium- to high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) recovered from four Antarctic sites (Whalers Bay, Crater Lake, Fumarole Bay, and Hannah Point) to investigate the relationship between geochemical gradients, biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Integrating genome-resolved metagenomics, biosynthetic mining, resistome profiling,
papers.summary: This study analyzed 319 metagenome-assembled genomes from four Antarctic sites to show that environmental filtering—driven by geochemical gradients—shapes both the biosynthetic potential (biosynthetic gene clusters) and the resistome (antimicrobial resistance genes) of Antarctic microbiomes. The findings reveal that local environmental conditions, rather than phylogeny alone, are key determinants of secondary metabolite production and antibiotic resistance in these extreme ecosystems.

papers.title: Blood and gut virome remodeling in gastric cancer: Anellovirus expansion and novel virus discovery.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a prevalent malignancy worldwide, yet effective early diagnostic tools remain lacking, and the role of the virome, a key component of the tumor microenvironment, in GC progression is largely unknown. This study aimed to characterize the virome landscapes in peripheral blood and feces of GC patients versus healthy controls, and to identify viral signatures associated with GC onset and metastasis. We performed viral metagenomic sequencing on pooled libraries from 100 GC patients (45 non-metastatic, 55 metastatic) and 50 healthy controls, followed by taxonomic annotation, d
papers.summary: This study characterizes the blood and gut virome in gastric cancer patients using viral metagenomic sequencing, revealing an expansion of Anellovirus and the discovery of novel viruses associated with cancer onset and metastasis. These findings suggest that virome alterations could serve as potential biomarkers for gastric cancer.

papers.title: Drought stress adaptation in Ficus carica L.: Modulation of ROS scavenging, nitrogen uptake, and rhizosphere bacterial community assembly and functions.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms are crucial for plant drought resistance; however, their response to drought stress in fig plants remains poorly understood. In this study, potted 'BoJi Red' fig plants were utilized to systematically investigate drought-induced changes in the structure, assembly processes, and functional potential of rhizosphere bacterial communities. The results showed that drought significantly inhibited fig growth, photosynthesis, and nitrogen uptake, while increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) content and antioxidant enzyme activities, although these enzyme activities decline
papers.summary: This study examines how drought stress affects fig plants and their rhizosphere bacterial communities, finding that drought inhibits growth, photosynthesis, and nitrogen uptake while altering bacterial community structure and assembly. The research highlights the role of rhizosphere microbes in plant drought adaptation and suggests potential targets for improving drought resistance in figs.

papers.title: AI-guided discovery of antimicrobial peptides for urinary tract infections leveraging a new catalogue of the human urinary microbiome.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are common infections that pose a critical burden on healthcare and society. Despite growing recognition that the human urinary tract harbors its own microbiome, its composition, functional potential, and alterations in UTI remain limited. Here, we leveraged the publicly available whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing data from 450 urinary microbiome samples collected in four independent cohorts together with genome assembly and metagenomic binning to construct an extensive human urinary microbiome catalog consisting of ∼1.3 million non-redundant microbial genes a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint constructs a comprehensive gene catalog of the human urinary microbiome from 450 metagenomic samples and uses AI-guided discovery to identify antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) with potential activity against urinary tract infections (UTIs). The work provides a new resource for understanding the urinary microbiome and demonstrates a computational approach for AMP discovery.

papers.title: Convergent Gut Microbiome Remodeling Across Ischemic Stroke, Myocardial Infarction, and Longevity Reveals a Shared Ecological Signature of Aging and Disease.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis has been associated with ischemic stroke (IS), myocardial infarction (MI), and aging, but whether these contexts share reproducible microbial features remains unclear. We conducted an exploratory and hypothesis-generating descriptive study of genus-level microbiota patterns across an internal IS cohort and publicly available external IS, MI, and age-stratified or longevity-associated datasets. Analyses were performed within predefined age strata and interpreted cautiously because of the small internal cohort, cross-cohort heterogeneity, and the absence of direct metabo
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiome changes are shared across ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and aging. By analyzing internal and public datasets, the authors identify a convergent ecological signature of dysbiosis common to these conditions, suggesting a shared microbial pattern linked to aging and disease.

papers.title: Robust and Interpretable Metagenomic Modeling Through Structure-Aware Multi-View Learning and Attribution-Guided Biological Insight.
papers.abstract: Integrative modeling of metagenomic and clinical data can advance the study of host phenotypes, but remains challenged by cross-view heterogeneity, uncertain generalizability, and poor interpretability. We developed SAMECAT (Structure-Aware Metagenomics multi-viEw Contrastive AlignmenT), a structure-aware deep learning framework that integrates species-level shotgun metagenomic profiles with mixed-type clinical covariates through view-specific encoders, clustering-informed contrastive alignment, and adaptive representation fusion. Using two independent Louisiana Osteoporosis Study datasets gen
papers.summary: SAMECAT is a new deep learning framework that integrates species-level metagenomic profiles with mixed-type clinical data using structure-aware multi-view learning and contrastive alignment, improving robustness and interpretability. Applied to two independent osteoporosis datasets, it demonstrates enhanced predictive performance and provides attribution-guided biological insights, addressing key challenges in metagenomic-clinical integrative modeling.

papers.title: Optimized Controlled-Release Fertilization Improves Productivity and Reshapes the Rhizosphere Microbiome in Lei Bamboo: A Metagenomic Assessment.
papers.abstract: Intensive nitrogen fertilization in Lei bamboo (Phyllostachys praecox) plantations has increased productivity but has also reduced nitrogen-use efficiency (NUE), accelerated nutrient losses, and contributed to soil degradation. How nutrient-release strategies influence rhizosphere microbiome assembly and ecosystem functioning remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a bamboo shoot-specific controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) and evaluated different urea-CRF blending ratios to identify sustainable fertilization strategy for Lei bamboo production. Mixed CRF-urea treatments outperformed both
papers.summary: This study developed a controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) for Lei bamboo and tested different blends with urea to improve productivity and sustainability. Metagenomic analysis revealed that optimized CRF-urea ratios reshaped the rhizosphere microbiome, enhancing nitrogen-use efficiency and soil health compared to intensive nitrogen fertilization alone.

papers.title: Genome-Resolved Metagenomics Reveals Thermophilic Microbial Diversity and Putative Hydrolase-Encoding Genes in the El Tatio Geothermal Field.
papers.abstract: Geothermal ecosystems constitute important reservoirs of thermophilic microorganisms and their associated metabolic functions; however, the genome-resolved diversity and enzymatic potential of high-altitude geothermal systems remain poorly characterized. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to investigate thermophilic microbial communities inhabiting geothermal sediments from the El Tatio geothermal field, a polyextreme hydrothermal system located at ~4300 m above sea level in the Andean Altiplano of northern Chile. Genome reconstruction yielded 657 metagenome-a
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to characterize thermophilic microbial communities in the El Tatio geothermal field, a high-altitude Andean hydrothermal system. The authors reconstructed 657 metagenome-assembled genomes, revealing novel microbial diversity and identifying putative hydrolase-encoding genes with potential biotechnological applications.

papers.title: De novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes with nf-core/mag.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA provides a direct window into the evolutionary processes that have shaped living microbial species today, as well as their now extinct relatives. Advances in both sequencing methods and de novo assembly techniques have not only resulted in a flood of modern metagenomic sequencing data, but they have also allowed palaeogenomicists to retrieve vast amounts of ancient DNA from past microorganisms, including species and strains without modern reference genomes. However, the degraded nature of ancient DNA means that the standard techniques of genome assembly developed for modern DNA are
papers.summary: This paper presents nf-core/mag, a new bioinformatics pipeline for de novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes, addressing the unique challenges of degraded DNA. The pipeline integrates standard metagenomic assembly with authentication steps to distinguish authentic ancient microbial DNA from modern contamination, providing a valuable tool for palaeogenomic studies.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and hormonomic insights into cadmium tolerance of a Euglena mutabilis fungal-algal-bacterial consortium.
papers.abstract: Acidic, metal-contaminated environments harbour specialized microbial consortia adapted to extreme stress. We examined an environmental Euglena mutabilis culture naturally associated with Talaromyces and Acidiphilium acidophilum and exposed it to cadmium (Cd). Integrated transcriptomic, hormonal, structural and taxonomic analyses revealed a coordinated Cd-tolerance strategy. RNA sequencing showed differential regulation of metal transporters consistent with a shift from Cd uptake to intracellular sequestration. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed Cd compartmentalization within chloropla
papers.summary: This study reveals how a microbial consortium centered on the alga Euglena mutabilis tolerates cadmium stress through a coordinated strategy of reduced uptake and intracellular sequestration, as shown by integrated transcriptomic and hormonal analyses. The findings highlight the potential of such natural consortia for bioremediation in metal-contaminated environments.

papers.title: Maternal and Infant Skin Microbiome Synchrony and Divergence: A Longitudinal Study of Skin Microbial Ecology and Early-Life Assembly.
papers.abstract: During pregnancy and after childbirth, women's skin undergoes significant changes which may affect the skin's functional and structural characteristics and microbial diversity. Like their mothers, the newborns also experience various skin challenges in the months following birth. Temporal changes in skin microbiome in special groups such as pregnant women and newborns, as well as the interrelation between their skin's microbial diversity, have not been investigated. We followed women from pregnancy through 6 months after delivery, and their infants from 4 weeks to 6 months of age to investigat
papers.summary: This longitudinal study tracks skin microbiome changes in mothers from pregnancy through 6 months postpartum and in their infants from 4 weeks to 6 months of age, revealing both synchrony and divergence in microbial diversity between maternal and infant skin. The findings highlight how maternal skin microbial ecology influences early-life assembly of the infant skin microbiome, with implications for understanding skin health and development.

papers.title: Insights Into Boar Semen Under Tropical Conditions in Smallholder Production Systems: Semen Quality, Potential Microbiota Contamination and Antimicrobial Susceptibility.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated boar semen quality, seminal microbiome composition, and antimicrobial susceptibility of bacteria isolated from seminal plasma in a tropical smallholder pig production system in Indonesia. A total of 10 ejaculates were collected from eight sexually mature boars using the gloved-hand technique from two herds located in East Nusa Tenggara (Herd A) and East Java (Herd B). Semen quality was evaluated using conventional methods in Herd A (five ejaculates from three boars) and a mobile semen analysis unit in Herd B (five ejaculates from five boars). Seminal microbiome composition
papers.summary: This study assessed semen quality, seminal microbiome, and antimicrobial resistance in boars from smallholder tropical farms in Indonesia. It found that semen quality varied between herds and identified potential bacterial contamination with notable antimicrobial resistance, highlighting the need for improved hygiene and monitoring in smallholder systems.

papers.title: 2'-FL's Depiction of the Human Physiological Function Landscape.
papers.abstract: 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) is a major fucosylated human milk oligosaccharide characterized by a terminal α1,2-linked fucose residue, which supports its interactions with gut microbes, host glycan-recognition systems, and pathogen-binding sites. This review proposes that 2'-FL acts mainly through a hierarchical host-microbiota mechanism: it first shapes gut microbial composition, then influences microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, and subsequently contributes to intestinal barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, and broader physiological outcomes. Current evidence is strongest
papers.summary: This review proposes that 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL), a major human milk oligosaccharide, acts through a hierarchical host-microbiota mechanism: first shaping gut microbial composition, then influencing microbial metabolites like short-chain fatty acids, and subsequently contributing to intestinal barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, and broader physiological outcomes. The paper maps the current evidence for 2'-FL's effects across multiple physiological systems, highlighting its potential health benefits.

papers.title: Cross sectional analysis of gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study investigated the differences in gut microbiota in patients with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), exploring their cross-sectional associations with nutritional intake.
papers.summary: This study compared the gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without a percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) feeding tube, finding differences in microbial composition that were associated with nutritional intake. The results suggest that the method of nutritional support may influence the gut microbiome in ALS patients, potentially impacting disease progression or management.

papers.title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and functional alterations in Campylobacter-associated gastroenteritis using metagenomic approaches.
papers.abstract: Campylobacter species are a major cause of bacterial gastroenteritis worldwide. Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from PCR-confirmed Campylobacter-positive patients and symptomatic PCR-negative controls, we reveal dysbiosis marked by reduced species richness (median Shannon diversity was significantly lower in the Campylobacter-positive group [3.24] vs. Campylobacter-negative group [3.63], P = 0.038), taxonomic shifts toward inflammation-associated taxa (Campylobacteriaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, Pasteurellaceae), and depletion of key commensals involved in short-chain fatty
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize gut microbiome dysbiosis in Campylobacter-associated gastroenteritis, finding reduced species diversity and shifts toward inflammation-associated taxa with depletion of beneficial commensals. The results provide insights into functional alterations of the gut microbiome during Campylobacter infection.

papers.title: Bioinformatic tools for microbiome analysis: from raw sequences to biological insights.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of microbiome research has been accompanied by an expanding but fragmented ecosystem of bioinformatic tools. Researchers now face a daunting array of software packages, pipelines, and web platforms spanning every stage of analysis, from quality control and taxonomic profiling to functional annotation and statistical interpretation. While this diversity offers flexibility, it also creates challenges in selecting appropriate tools and integrating them into coherent, reproducible workflows, particularly for researchers without formal computational training. This review presents a
papers.summary: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the bioinformatics tools available for microbiome analysis, covering the entire pipeline from raw sequencing data to biological interpretation. It highlights the challenges researchers face in choosing and integrating these tools into reproducible workflows, especially for those without computational expertise.

papers.title: Decoding the rhizosphere microbiome against Sclerotium rolfsii: integrating multi-omics and AI-driven predictive models.
papers.abstract: The soil-borne necrotrophic fungus Sclerotium rolfsii is a globally important pathogen causing collar rot, southern blight, and damping-off in diverse crops, resulting in substantial losses in yield, particularly during warm and cloudy weather. Through processes like niche competition, antibiosis, induced systemic resistance, and enzymatic destruction of pathogen propagules, there is mounting evidence that the rhizosphere microbiome is crucial in influencing disease outcomes. This systemic review synthesizes published evidence on rhizosphere microbial structure and function under S. rolfsii pr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on how the rhizosphere microbiome influences disease outcomes against the fungal pathogen Sclerotium rolfsii, highlighting mechanisms like niche competition, antibiosis, and induced systemic resistance. It advocates for integrating multi-omics data with AI-driven predictive models to decode microbiome-mediated suppression and improve crop protection strategies.

papers.title: Gut microbiota of sprint athletes: signature microbes and dietary links.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota has emerged as an important biological factor associated with host physiological status in athletes. However, relevant research remains limited for sprint athletes, whose physiological demands differ substantially from those of endurance athletes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbiota of sprint athletes, identifying signature microbial taxa and their associations with dietary intake, which differ from those seen in endurance athletes. The findings highlight the unique gut microbiome composition linked to sprint-specific physiology and nutrition.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived imidazole propionate is associated with obesity.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a progressive metabolic disorder with some well-recognized markers, such as increased or elevated branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). However, the role of gut microbiota-derived metabolites remains unknown in Asian populations. By employing an integrated multi-omics approach combining metagenomic and plasma metabolomic profiling in an Asian cohort alongside a longitudinal analysis of a bariatric surgery subgroup. We identified a distinct metabolic signature in obesity characterized by depleted circulating histidine and a concomitant elevation of Imidazole Propionate (ImP). The eleva
papers.summary: This study identifies a distinct metabolic signature in obesity among Asian individuals, characterized by depleted circulating histidine and elevated gut microbiota-derived imidazole propionate (ImP). Using an integrated multi-omics approach with metagenomic and plasma metabolomic profiling, the findings suggest ImP as a potential marker for obesity, with implications for understanding host-microbiome interactions in metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Ecosystem settings and urbanization shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on coastal microplastics.
papers.abstract: Coastal wetlands are increasingly contaminated by microplastics that provide long-lived substrates for microbial colonization, yet the joint effects of ecosystem settings and urbanization on plastisphere communities and their resistomes remain poorly understood. Here, we used a 2 × 2 factorial design across mangrove and sandy-beach sediments under rural and urban influence, combined with metagenomic profiling, to characterize microplastic-associated microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Microbial communities on microplastics showed clear separation between mangroves and sandy shor
papers.summary: This study investigates how ecosystem type (mangrove vs. sandy beach) and urbanization level (rural vs. urban) jointly shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on microplastics in coastal wetlands. Using a factorial design and metagenomic profiling, the authors found that both factors significantly influence the composition of the plastisphere and its resistome, with distinct separation between mangroves and sandy shores.

papers.title: Effect of phosphorus fraction in shaping bacterial and archaeal community succession in the largest hydrologically connected lake of Northeast Asia.
papers.abstract: Microbial beta diversity and its components are key ecological indicators for understanding community assembly in lake sediments, yet their coupling with phosphorus (P) fractions remains poorly understood in hydrologically connected lake systems. In this study, sediment cores were collected from Xingkai Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Northeast Asia with a unique twin lake structure, and were analyzed using metagenomic sequencing combined with sequential P fractionation. Results showed that total beta diversity and species turnover for bacteria and archaea increased significantly with sed
papers.summary: This study examines how phosphorus fractions shape bacterial and archaeal community succession in the sediments of Xingkai Lake, the largest hydrologically connected lake in Northeast Asia. Using metagenomic sequencing and phosphorus fractionation, the authors found that total beta diversity and species turnover increased with sediment depth, with specific phosphorus fractions playing a key role in driving microbial community assembly.

papers.title: From natural assemblages to synthetic communities in the Lupinus microbiome.
papers.abstract: Plant roots harbour complex microbial communities that enhance nutrient acquisition, stress tolerance, and pathogen defence, yet their assembly and functional dynamics remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the Lupinus (lupin) root microbiome, from natural field assemblages to the construction of synthetic microbial communities, highlighting how these approaches can reveal mechanisms of microbiome assembly and function. It emphasizes the potential of synthetic communities to translate natural microbiome insights into practical applications for improving lupin nutrient acquisition and stress resilience.

papers.title: Characterization of the intestinal microbial profile in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) are major contributors to dementia, with growing prevalence in Latin America. Evidence suggests that gut microbiota alterations may influence neurodegeneration, but data on Hispanic population are lacking.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbial profile in patients with mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on a Hispanic population where such data were previously lacking. It likely identifies specific microbial alterations associated with cognitive decline, supporting the link between gut microbiota and neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Differential gut microbiota modulation associated with anti-Parkinsonian effects of Ophiopogon japonicus across geographical origins and extraction methods.
papers.abstract: Ophiopogon japonicus (OJ) is a medicine-food homologous plant widely consumed in East Asia and has attracted attention for its potential anti-Parkinsonian properties. However, the influence of geographical origin and extraction methods on its bioactive profile, gut microbiota modulation, and anti-Parkinsonian effects remain insufficiently understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the geographical origin and extraction method of Ophiopogon japonicus (OJ) affect its anti-Parkinsonian properties, focusing on gut microbiota modulation. The findings reveal that different OJ preparations differentially alter gut microbial composition, which correlates with varying neuroprotective effects, highlighting the importance of standardization for therapeutic use.

papers.title: Microbial colonisation of the neonatal beef calf gastrointestinal tract: limited influence of birth delivery method across five anatomical regions.
papers.abstract: The microbiome assembly of the neonatal gastrointestinal tract is critical for immune and metabolic development, and birth delivery method can influence initial microbial colonisation. Using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, we investigated the effect of transvaginal and elective caesarean section delivery on microbial composition across five gastrointestinal regions (colon, ileum, jejunum, meconium, and rumen) in Aberdeen Angus calves (transvaginal, TV; n = 12; caesarean section, CS; n = 10) across two research farms. Absolute microbial quantities were measured using 16S rRNA qPCR. Alpha div
papers.summary: This study examines how birth delivery method (transvaginal vs. caesarean section) affects the early gut microbiome of beef calves across five gastrointestinal regions. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and qPCR, the authors found that delivery method had only a limited influence on microbial colonisation, suggesting other factors may play a larger role in neonatal gut microbiome assembly in cattle.

papers.title: Assessment of gut microbiota dynamics and probiotic impact on HPV-associated head and neck cancer using 16S rRNA sequencing and cytokine profiling.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major etiological factor in head and neck cancers, primarily through the oncogenic activities of viral proteins E6 and E7, which disrupt the p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) tumor suppressor pathways. This disruption promotes uncontrolled cell proliferation, immune dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and malignant transformation. Although probiotics have emerged as promising modulators of the microbiome and host immune responses, their mechanistic role in HPV-associated head and neck cancer remains insufficiently understood. Therefore, this study investigated the th
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study examines how gut microbiota composition and probiotic intervention affect HPV-associated head and neck cancer, using 16S rRNA sequencing and cytokine profiling. The findings suggest that probiotics may modulate the gut microbiome and immune responses, potentially offering a supportive role in managing this cancer type, though the mechanistic details remain to be fully clarified.

papers.title: Preoperative gut microbiota combined with machine learning for predicting post-hepatectomy liver failure in HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the association between preoperative gut microbiota (GM) profiles and post-hepatectomy liver failure (PHLF) in patients with newly diagnosed HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC), aiming to explore non-invasive, modifiable GM biomarkers for perioperative risk stratification.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This pilot study explores whether preoperative gut microbiota profiles can predict post-hepatectomy liver failure in patients with HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma. Using machine learning, the authors identify potential microbial biomarkers that could serve as non-invasive, modifiable tools for perioperative risk stratification.

papers.title: Genetic predictive links between oropharyngeal microecology and obstructive sleep apnea syndrome: expanding the perspective of etiology.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS), a global public health concern, is linked to oropharyngeal microbiota, but observational studies cannot confirm their causal association.
papers.summary: This study uses genetic data to investigate whether oropharyngeal microbiota composition is causally linked to obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS), moving beyond observational correlations. The findings suggest potential causal relationships between specific microbial taxa and OSAS risk, offering new insights into the etiology of the disease.

papers.title: Dietary sulforaphane in cancer chemoprevention: epigenetic regulation and PRMT5-MEP50 complex inhibition-a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Cancer chemoprevention using dietary bioactive compounds has emerged as a promising, cost-effective strategy to reduce global cancer incidence and mortality. Sulforaphane (SFN), an isothiocyanate abundant in cruciferous vegetables, has attracted considerable attention for its pleiotropic anticancer effects.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines the chemopreventive mechanisms of sulforaphane (SFN), a compound found in cruciferous vegetables, focusing on its epigenetic regulation and inhibition of the PRMT5-MEP50 complex. The findings suggest that SFN exerts anticancer effects through multiple pathways, including modulation of histone modifications and DNA methylation, as well as direct inhibition of oncogenic protein complexes.

papers.title: Effects of probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics on lung function and symptoms in adults with bronchial asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics may exert beneficial effects on asthma by modulating the gut microbiota and the "gut-lung axis". However, no systematic review or meta-analysis has specifically focused on adult asthma patients.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effects of probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics on lung function and symptoms in adults with bronchial asthma, focusing on the gut-lung axis. The findings provide evidence on whether these interventions improve asthma outcomes in this specific population.

papers.title: From Gut to Brain: Probiotics as an Emerging Adjunctive Strategy for Insomnia and Sleep Disturbances.
papers.abstract: Too little sleep and incidental insomnia are two common conditions in which sleep is disrupted. Insomnia is often accompanied by emotional, metabolic, and immunological deterioration. The purpose of this narrative review is to better understand the gut-brain axis and evaluate the potential usefulness of probiotics in the treatment of insomnia and related sleep problems.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the gut-brain axis and evaluates the potential of probiotics as an adjunctive treatment for insomnia and sleep disturbances. It synthesizes current evidence suggesting that modulating the gut microbiome may improve sleep quality and associated emotional, metabolic, and immunological outcomes.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of gut microbiota, plasma metabolome, and gene expression identifies causal mediators in Graves' disease pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Graves' disease (GD) is characterized by hyperthyroidism and is influenced by genetic and environmental factors. The "gut-thyroid axis" establishes a connection between the gut microbiota and GD, yet the underlying potential mechanisms remain unclear. This study employed Mendelian randomization to investigate the causal relationships between the gut microbiota and GD, aiming to identify key microbial taxa and their metabolites, as well as to explore the regulatory roles of relevant genes in the pathogenesis of GD.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to investigate causal links between gut microbiota and Graves' disease, identifying specific microbial taxa, their metabolites, and regulatory genes that may mediate pathogenesis via the gut-thyroid axis. The findings provide new insights into potential mechanisms and targets for Graves' disease.

papers.title: Integrating tongue coating microbiome, tongue coating metabolomics, and exhaled breath metabolomics via machine learning to identify chronic atrophic gastritis.
papers.abstract: Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous gastric condition with limited non-invasive diagnostic options. Alterations in the oral microbiome and its localized metabolic profiles may provide early multi-omics signatures of disease progression.
papers.summary: This study integrates tongue coating microbiome, tongue coating metabolomics, and exhaled breath metabolomics using machine learning to identify non-invasive biomarkers for chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG), a precancerous gastric condition. The multi-omics approach reveals distinct microbial and metabolic alterations associated with CAG, offering a promising strategy for early diagnosis.
